findings.name: Best compressed method in 20/20 settings, +5.9% over SentenceKV at 10% KV budget

abaskohi2026sekv.basis: Spans, summaries and SVD factors are written from surprisal before any query, so the writer is query-agnostic; the query-dependent zoom gate is a read-side addressing step. No ablation separates routing misses from low-rank write error, so Addressing and Write are I, and the gap to full KV (and the comparison with eviction) is Unassigned (Addressing, Write distortion). Revision: the study reports loss at a reduced budget against a larger one, which confounds Capacity, so Capacity is U, not '-'.

findings.name: Soft tokens keep topic but lose dates and numbers; reconstruction hallucinates facts
Compression sharply lowers grounding (FABLES), most for xRAG

All methods lose about half of multi-hop HotpotQA EM
Compressed GSM8K examples do worse than no examples

ajewska2025understanding.basis: The paper trains its own xRAG variants, and every compressor it evaluates encodes documents without the query, so it has a writer and is query-agnostic. Reconstruction probes point to Write distortion, but they are confounded with how the decoder reads and are not compared at equal compression ratios, so Write is I. The HotpotQA and GSM8K drops are Unassigned (Write distortion vs residual or interference). Revision: the study reports loss at a reduced budget against a larger one, which confounds Capacity, so Capacity is U, not '-'. After independent grading: Table 6 compares writer variants (sentence and two-step pre-training) at the same number of encodings, isolating Write distortion at equal budget.

findings.name: Long-distance relative positions are rarely seen in pretraining (i≥1536 under 5% of indices at L=2048)
Effective context length follows position frequency, not maximum training length
Distant needles are not retrieved; failures concentrate in the first L/3 of the document across 13 models
STRING raises 4-needle NIAH (85.7 vs 67.8 RoPE) and RULER at 128K (Llama3.1-70B 66.6 to 81.7; Qwen2-72B 53.7 to 84.6), while YaRN, DCA, Self-Extend and ReRoPE do not help within the training length
On InfiniteBench, Llama3.1-70B with STRING (56.88) beats GPT-4 (55.69)
At least the last third of position indices can be overwritten without loss

an2024effective.basis: STRING reads the full uncompressed context, which is written with no query filtering (query-agnostic, no budget), and changes only the query position ids while all content stays fixed. That is positional under-use, so Addressing. The notes come from a full-text reading, so the abstract-only cap does not apply, but Addressing is still graded I because the intervention shifts positions for all tokens and there is no count-matched sham that raises access to non-answer content.

findings.name: Gated convolutions need model dimension d ≥ N to solve Mqar; attention does not
Required recurrent state dimension grows with the number of key-value pairs to recall
AR hits explain 82% of the perplexity gap to attention, worst on rare bigrams
RWKV degrades as the number of queries grows
Sparse input-dependent attention closes 72–85% of the AR gap

arora2023zoology.basis: As the reviewer says, this is a fixed-state bound on the sequence model itself, like Jelassi et al., so the substrate is architecture, there is no writer, and there is no reuse flag. Capacity is B from the Mqar dimension result. The Pile perplexity gaps are measured errors of real systems that confound capacity with input-dependent routing, so they are Unassigned.

findings.name: Evicted entries become permanently inaccessible; accumulated score biased toward the least recent tokens
At a 20% budget H2O nearly matches full cache while recency-only eviction collapses
Sink-plus-recent streaming loses mid-context information
Masking heavy hitters drastically hurts accuracy
Recency-only eviction degenerates generated text

barrett2023h2o.basis: H2O scores entries with attention from past queries, so it is proxy-query. Its comparison with recency-only eviction falls under rule 5 with no item-by-item or count-matched control, so Addressing is I (confound: it may win by dropping competitors). Write is '-' (the reviewer is right: retained entries are unaltered). The greedy guarantee is for a submodular surrogate, not a capacity bound. Revision: its gains over recency-only eviction compare a proxy-query writer with a query-agnostic one, so the comparison crosses query-knowledge classes and Addressing is U (Capacity, Addressing), not I.

findings.name: Heuristic eviction loses substantial accuracy at strict budgets (e.g., 512 tokens)
Oracle analysis defines theoretical bounds on accuracy, compute and storage

behnam2025empiric.basis: Read only in abstract, so no cell can exceed I and Table 1 marks it. The oracle's writer class is unstated, so its bounds cannot serve as a Capacity bound for any query-knowledge class. Capacity and Addressing are therefore U (confounded), and there is no writer of its own.

findings.name: Quality declines beyond ~2.5k context tokens (context cliff)
Abstention falls with larger context budget and rises with chunk size
Sentence and semantic chunking tie; token chunking lags; code chunking worst
20% overlap gives no quality gain but 1.25× more chunks

bennani2026systematic.basis: An end-to-end sweep of several chunkers with no writer of its own. Raising the context budget adds both answer-bearing chunks and distractors, and changing the chunking alters both what is stored and what is retrieved. Every finding therefore confounds Addressing, Interference and Write (U), and Section 5 may cite the context cliff only as Unassigned. No task bound exists: capacity floor unknown. Revision: the study reports loss at a reduced budget against a larger one, which confounds Capacity, so Capacity is U, not '-'.

findings.name: Near-tie distractors drive attention mass on useful tokens toward zero (Proposition 3.1)
Eviction matches or beats full-cache inference on VLM reasoning, MMDU and LongBench-v2

bui2026make.basis: The retention score is computed once from the token embedding when the token enters the cache, so the writer is query-agnostic; the cache serves later turns in multi-turn dialogue (reuse flag). Proposition 3.1 is an argument about softmax dilution, not a bound on this system's loss, and no ablation isolates dilution, so Interference is I. The wins over heuristics fall under rule 5 without controls, so Addressing is I. Revision: the study reports loss at a reduced budget against a larger one, which confounds Capacity, so Capacity is U, not '-'. After independent grading: reports gains over SnapKV and Ada-KV at the same budget, an Addressing lower bound under rule 5.

findings.name: Stability horizon unbounded while access and utility horizons are finite (constructive)
Attention sinks keep local modeling but not content beyond the active cache
Recurrent and retrieval state extend the semantic horizon
Anchor tokens should not be treated as semantic memory

cao2026separating.basis: Read in abstract only, so no cell can be above I. The construction does not bound the best store, so content lost beyond the cache is Unassigned (Capacity, Addressing). The contract spans KV, recurrent and retrieval state, so the substrate is 'several' and the study defines no writer.

findings.name: Accuracy drops as noise ratio rises to 0.8 (five documents fixed)

Strict vs judged rejection gap (instruction following; residual)

chen2023benchmarking.basis: Raising the noise ratio also lowers the number of positive documents among the fixed five, and no similarity-matched control exists. So noise losses are Unassigned (Addressing, Interference), and the Sec. 5 table row must say Unassigned, not crosstalk. Passages come from a retrieval index (external index). Counterfactual documents are altered stored items (rule 4), graded I because the study compares them with parametric answers, not with correct documents.

findings.name: Fano bound: every layer errs below the task information requirement
Query-agnostic operator pays a budget penalty of about H(Q)

Near-lossless on easy tasks, failing on high-information tasks
Practical compressibility far exceeds worst-case bounds

colaco2026keep.basis: The Fano bound and the B−H(Q) penalty give Capacity B. The eviction collapse is not compared against the bound, so it is Unassigned (Capacity, Addressing), and Addressing is therefore U rather than '-'. Interference stays '-' because no result involves competitors. The summarization drift under repeated compaction is our inference (I), since the operators differ in more than write fidelity.

findings.name: One distracting passage sharply cuts accuracy; more distractors degrade progressively

Random passages triple attention entropy

cuconasu2024power.basis: Distracting and random passages are compared at the same count with the gold passage and its position fixed. That is the ledger's replace-with-dissimilar test, so Interference is M, and the Sec. 5 line 'suggestive but undecomposed' must be revised. Addressing M rests on the direct answer-in-top-k measurement for BM25 vs Contriever. The position effect is measured only with distractors present and has no sham control, so it stays Unassigned. Revision: distracting and random passages are compared at the same count and the same gold positions (far/mid/near), which is the Interference test, so Interference is M; our earlier position-confound objection was wrong.

The Sec. 8 'Addr (access)' label must change. The selector changes the read at a fixed store and k with no item-level control, so under rule 5 it is Addressing I, not M. The store is agent memory text written by scenarios, not by a system writer of the study's own.

Group size 128 degrades GSM8K (17.29 vs 20.77 at 32)
Long-context accuracy nearly preserved at 2 bits (Mistral-7B LongBench 45.85 vs 46.58)

liu2024kivi.basis: Matched-bit layout ablations (per-token vs per-channel, residual window, group size) isolate the quantization error, so Write distortion is M. The addressing reading (key error that distorts attention scores) is ours and is not tested, so Addressing is I, which matches the draft's statement that the addressing reading is untested. Revision: the study reports loss at a reduced budget against a larger one, which confounds Capacity, so Capacity is U, not '-'.

findings.name: Higher LongBench average than Quest and InfiniGen at every budget, close to full KV (48.7 at 2048 vs 49.01)
Token importance changes during decoding, which motivates recallable rather than permanent eviction
Page-based recall wastes budget: a 16-token page holds one or two important tokens
Perplexity deviation up to 0.5 at budget 1024 vs about 4 (Quest) and 2 (InfiniGen)
Recall of true top-B tokens stays below 1 (about 0.2-0.5); cosine clustering recalls best, with gains levelling off above 400 clusters

liu2025clusterkv.basis: Keys are clustered at prefill without the query, and the full KV stays offloaded. The write is therefore query-agnostic, the store is reused across decoding steps, and the query-dependent choice is a read-time address decision. The gains over Quest and InfiniGen are same-budget policy comparisons without item-level evidence or a count-matched control, so under rule 5 Addressing is I (possible confound: the better policy may have won by dropping competitors). Revision: the study reports loss at a reduced budget against a larger one, which confounds Capacity, so Capacity is U, not '-'.

findings.name: All models lag humans far behind on QA (GPT-4-turbo 32.1 vs human 87.9)
Long-context models misattribute dialogs or events to the wrong speaker and hallucinate
RAG over observations works best overall (41.4) and on temporal questions
Summary retrieval has high recall (90.7) but low F1 (31.5), attributed to information lost in summarization
16K model is below the 4K model on event summarization (FactScore F1 39.9 vs 45.9)
Inaccurate retrieval adds improper context and hurts open-domain questions

maharana2024evaluating.basis: LoCoMo is a benchmark that evaluates several writers, so it has no write-time label and no reuse flag. Following the ledger's substrate rule, it is filed as natural-language text because the memories under discussion (observations and recursive summaries) are rewritten as text. None of its comparisons isolates a term (the summary loss is the authors' 'likely' explanation, and the top-k dilution has no count-matched control), so every non-capacity grade is I, and capacity has no bound. Revision: the study reports loss at a reduced budget against a larger one, which confounds Capacity, so Capacity is U, not '-'.

findings.name: H2O exact match collapses from 88% to 0% at a 5% budget on schema-dense QA
DELIM tokens act as a distributed attention sink (mass 13.64 vs 0.336 for VALUE, about 674 positions)
H2O keeps KEY tokens 1.94x as often as VALUE tokens at B=5% on JSON, consistently across four model families and in the base model
Banning KEY tokens recovers accuracy (0.82 vs 0.14 at B=0.50); banning DELIM or VALUE is catastrophic
Role-conditional allocator reaches 0.56 at B=0.05 vs SnapKV 0.20 and H2O 0.02
SnapKV's max-pool acts as implicit sink suppression; disabling it drops low-budget EM to 0.16
Margin above full cache is seed-sensitive (+0.01, CI [-0.03, +0.07] at B=0.30)
Linear role probe is 99.5% accurate in isolation but cuts downstream EM by 18-32 points
Gains vanish on sparse-role corpora (all alpha curves in a 0.55-0.66 band)

mandal2026adaptive.basis: Retention is reported per role, not per answer item, and there is no count-matched control: the allocator also keeps fewer KEY and DELIM competitors, and the harness masks the cache rather than compacting it. Under rule 5, Addressing is therefore I, and the KEY-ban ablation (which both drops competitors and frees budget for VALUE tokens) is Unassigned (Addressing, Interference). This replaces the draft's M in the Section 8 table. SnapKV's end-of-prompt observation window makes the writer proxy-query.

findings.name: StreamingLLM's sink-and-recency importance deviates substantially from true future-attention ranking
StreamingLLM perplexity rises sharply as the budget shrinks
Trained on ~4K tokens, KVP extrapolates to RULER-128K and beats every baseline at every budget
On OASST2, KVP has lower perplexity than other attention-free baselines except LagKV at the smallest budgets
KVP's eviction cost matches TOVA and SnapKV without using query information
Supervised ranking losses overfit attention sinks or mis-order top tokens at tight budgets; RL avoids this
Policies specialize to their training distribution (KVPS vs KVPR on zero-shot tasks)
KVP beats the learned baseline JudgeQ at every budget on three long-context benchmarks

moschella2026learning.basis: Agents score tokens from keys, values and position only, so the writer is query-agnostic. All gains come from same-budget policy comparisons with no item-level eviction evidence or count-matched control, so Addressing is I under rule 5. Comparisons with TOVA and SnapKV also cross query-knowledge classes, which shifts the capacity floor. Revision: the study reports loss at a reduced budget against a larger one, which confounds Capacity, so Capacity is U, not '-'.

findings.name: One gist token matches the uncompressed model on seen prompts but degrades on OOD human prompts (LLaMA 84.9%, FLAN-T5 63.2% retention)
Exact agreement with the uncompressed model falls from about 50% (seen) to about 10% (OOD human)
More gist tokens do not help and can hurt (LLaMA-7B, 10 gists), possibly through overfitting
At the same rate, TF-IDF keyword compression barely beats the negative control
Authors acknowledge an inherent loss of instruction nuance (e.g. 'Arts & Culture' becomes 'Culture')

mu2023learning.basis: Gists are learned KV prefixes computed from the instruction without the later input and cached across inputs. The write is therefore query-agnostic with multi-query reuse. No bound or ablation separates encoder error from the k-token budget limit, so Capacity and Write distortion are both U, as in the draft's 'Unassigned (Write distortion vs Capacity)'.

findings.name: Query-aware compression has a much lower distortion-rate limit than query-agnostic compression
Variable-rate query-aware limit is at least as good as fixed rate across queries
Pruning-only and tokenization-free optima are nearly identical to the general optimum
Most existing methods sit far from the limit; only Adaptive QuerySelect beats the query-agnostic optimum
On NarrativeQA the gap between methods and the query-aware bound is large, even for query-aware methods
The gap to the optimum depends on the query; Adaptive QuerySelect matches it on the palindrome query

nagle2024fundamental.basis: The linear-program distortion-rate function is a formal bound per writer class, so Capacity is B. It is theory, so it carries no write-time label even though it also proposes Adaptive QuerySelect. Because pruning-only is near optimal, a method's gap at the same rate is a selection shortfall, graded I as in the draft. Optimal compression beating the full prompt suggests that removed content perturbs reads, which we read as Interference (I).

findings.name: Paged access to full history beats lossy-summary baselines on deep memory retrieval (GPT-4 92.5% vs 32.1%)
Document truncation lowers fixed-context QA as the gold snippet is more often omitted
Fixed-context baselines are capped at roughly the retriever's recall
MemGPT often stops paging before exhausting retriever results
Weaker controllers (GPT-4 Turbo, GPT-3.5) drop off at 2 nesting levels by making too few lookups
Baselines with all KV pairs in context collapse on nested lookups (0% by 1-3 levels), while MemGPT with GPT-4 is unaffected

packer2023memgpt.basis: Under the ledger's substrate rule, agent memory written as text is natural-language text, whatever the paging mechanism. Facts and summaries are saved under memory pressure, before any future query is known, and are reused across sessions. The DMR gain confounds the baseline's lossy summary (write) with budget and read mechanism, so Write is U. Early stopping and too few lookups are observed but not isolated, so Addressing is I. Nested-lookup failures with gold pairs in context are residual, so they are left unassigned. Revision: the study reports loss at a reduced budget against a larger one, which confounds Capacity, so Capacity is U, not '-'.

findings.name: Most C→W failures have low or partial evidence coverage (63.2%)
Drift with structural addressability (ThinK/quantization) in 2,126 failures (17.0%)
All ten diagnostics separate failed from successful compression (AUROC 0.684–0.871)
Evidence-attention boost repairs 28/96 low-EAR failures vs 6/96 for count-matched non-evidence boost
Similar aggregate scores hide C→W rates of 0.8–2.0% at light compression
Methods with similar mean scores fail on different sources (Jaccard ≤0.385)
ThinK 50% and 2-bit quantization collapse with severe likelihood drift
Evidence coverage falls as retention decreases
Coverage diagnoses transfer across models; quantization drift is model-specific

qiu2026kvdiagnosis.basis: The evidence boost is tested against a count-matched non-evidence boost with C→C controls, which meets the ledger tie-break, so Addressing is M. Coverage rows have no best-store reference (Capacity vs Addressing) and drift rows have no equal-bit reference (Write distortion vs Capacity), so those cells are U.

findings.name: Attention-reconstruction conv compression beats auto-encoding, BPTT and pooling (0.973 vs 0.984–0.996 bpc)
Lossy attention-reconstruction objective preferred over lossless one
Improves over TransformerXL on PG-19 (33.6 vs 36.3)
Compression loss an order of magnitude higher for word-level than character-level modelling
Model attends more to compressed memory than to oldest regular memory

rae2019compressive.basis: At write time the learned compression function sees only the old activations, not the future query, so the writer is query-agnostic. No bound and no equal-slot lossless reference exist, so losses stay Unassigned (Write distortion vs Capacity), as in the Section 6 table.

findings.name: Beats full context on LongMemEval with ~70x fewer tokens (71.2% vs 60.2%)
Single-session-assistant accuracy drops 17.7% after extraction
Knowledge-update handling depends on model strength
Incremental community updates drift from full recomputation
Contradicted facts invalidated, not deleted (design; not evaluated)
Slightly beats MemGPT and full conversation on DMR, which authors deem too small

rasmussen2025zep.basis: Extraction happens at ingest without the question, so the writer is query-agnostic. The LongMemEval gains and drops do not separate extraction loss, retrieval misses and full-context dilution, so the cells are U, in line with the ledger's caution about thin agent-memory evidence. Community drift is Write distortion by definition but was not measured against accuracy. Revision: the study reports loss at a reduced budget against a larger one, which confounds Capacity, so Capacity is U, not '-'.

findings.name: Higher unique-token coverage goes with higher score than SnapKV (94.5% vs 86.6%)
Baselines lose more coverage at 0.9 eviction than K-VEC
Largest gains at B=128 (44.57 vs 42.96; full cache 49.20)
Qasper and TREC drop most under eviction relative to full cache
Coverage-module ablation: Qasper 35.96 to 25.54 (caption budget mismatch)
Over-weighting coverage (λ=2.0) lowers score
Information-bottleneck bound ties coverage to mutual information (per-policy, not best store)
On par with HeadKV and above SnapKV on Needle-in-a-Haystack

roy2026coverage.basis: Under rule 5 the same-budget ablation has no item-level evidence that the answer-bearing token was evicted, and no count-matched control. Addressing is therefore I (not the M in the Section 8 table); K-VEC may have won by dropping redundant competitors. The IB bound does not bound the best store, so Capacity is U. The prefill observation window contains the LongBench question, so the writer is query-aware. Query knowledge is labelled by design: an observation-window scorer is proxy-query even when an evaluation puts the question inside the window.

findings.name: Best retriever+reranker reaches only Hits@10 0.7467 and Hits@4 0.6625
Reranking raises voyage-02 Hits@10 from 0.6506 to 0.7467 at the same k
Embedding choice moves Hits@10 from 0.1479 to 0.6718
GPT-4 accuracy 0.56 with retrieved vs 0.89 with gold chunks
Open LLMs score 0.32–0.36 even with gold chunks (residual)
Negation and chronological-order errors with gold evidence (residual)
Most queries need 2–4 evidence pieces

tang2024multihop.basis: Hits@k checks, item by item and at a fixed k, whether gold evidence that is in the index and fits in k is reached, so Addressing is M. The retrieved-vs-gold accuracy gap mixes misses and distractors (Addressing vs Interference). Gold-chunk failures are residual. After independent grading: same-k retriever and reranker comparisons record misses per item but show no item-level repair or count-matched control, so under rule 5 they are lower bounds (I).

findings.name: Memory agents degrade sharply on remembering from weekly to quarterly
LLM forgetting penalty shrinks (32.6 to 17.8) because history overflows the context
Memory agents' stale-reuse penalty grows (18.2 to 29.5)
Forgetting-aware FAMA changes system rankings
Recommendation errors mostly outdated memory not forgotten; reasoning errors incomplete retrieval
Memora demands far more consolidation and mutation than prior benchmarks

uddin2026recall.basis: Memora evaluates several writers and defines none of its own. FAMA and the error analysis do not separate stale reads (Interference) from missing updates (Write distortion), or overflow and partial retrieval (Capacity, Addressing), so every cell is U, matching the draft's Unassigned labels.

findings.name: Retention extends from under 20k to over 160k tokens vs MemoryLLM
Random dropping during compression loses tokens even on short inputs
Below full-attention Llama-3.1-8B on short LongBench (32.78 vs 35.81)
SnapKV-style cache struggles beyond 30k tokens

wang2025m.basis: Chunks are compressed into memory tokens without the query, so the writer is query-agnostic; the compressed pool is reused across queries. The 30% token recall is not tied to answer-bearing items, and M+ vs M+-Attn has no item-level control (rule 5), so Addressing is I. Compression loss stays Unassigned (Write distortion vs Capacity), and M+ vs MemoryLLM isolates no term.

findings.name: Accuracy declines log-linearly with updates per key, reaching 0% for mid-size models
Parameter size predicts IES; context length does not
At fixed input length, tracking 46 keys drops llama4-maverick below 5%
Longer values drive accuracy below 40% and then below 5%
Errors shift from adjacent to earliest values, then to hallucinations
Per-key forget prompts help by less than 10 points
Mock QA reset helps but accuracy still declines
Sequential updates give step-like failure at a model-specific threshold
CoT and MoE give no robustness gain

wang2025unable.basis: Rule 3 assigns superseded values that are read to Interference, and the errors are overwritten values. The sweeps vary competitor count, not similarity at a fixed count, so the tie-break test is not met and the grade is I (the 'boundary case' of Section 9), not M. There is no budget and no writer.

findings.name: MCTS selection beats Top-k (0.327), Bandit (0.362) and Beam Search (0.380) with 0.432 ROUGE-1 under a 1024-token budget (Table VI)
Search-chosen ordering gains 11-15% relative over highest-score-first; reversing the chosen order drops ROUGE-1 from 0.43 to 0.21
NaiveRAG stays flat at 0.327/0.333/0.328 ROUGE-1 at 1024/2048/8192 tokens

wang2026carrot.basis: Rule 5 (tightened): no item-by-item evidence that baselines dropped the answer-bearing chunk and no count-matched control, and CARROT explicitly removes redundant chunks, so its gains may be reduced Interference; Addressing is I, not M as Sec. 7 says. The flat NaiveRAG curve confounds positional under-use and dilution, so it is Unassigned (Addressing, Interference). Revision: the study reports loss at a reduced budget against a larger one, which confounds Capacity, so Capacity is U, not '-'.

findings.name: Sound per-(layer, head, step) upper bound on total variation between exact and quantized attention
Cross-layer error cancellation: KIVI-2bit distorts 21.9% of steps yet retrieves 95.8%; no single layer's pollution alone loses anything
Meter gating with exact page-in restores broken schemes (fp8 22.8 to 79.7 on hard RULER)

wei2026witcert.basis: The TV bound is a formal bound on attention displacement caused by quantization error, and the ledger allows B for any term, so Write is B. Gating pages in FP16 blocks and so changes bits per entry. It is Unassigned (Capacity, Write distortion), consistent with the Sec. 8 list of omitted comparisons.

findings.name: Training from scratch with large memory is unstable, possibly due to key staleness (authors' speculation)
About 90% approximate kNN recall; no significant degradation with lower-quality kNN (qualitative)
With larger memory some tokens get worse, possibly because a relevant memory leaves the top-k

wu2022memorizing.basis: The staleness claim is speculative and the kNN-quality result is qualitative with no item-level test, so Addressing is I, not M. The larger-memory result confounds a retrieval miss with being outcompeted by added entries, so it is Unassigned (Addressing, Interference), and the Interference cell is U. Revision: the study reports loss at a reduced budget against a larger one, which confounds Capacity, so Capacity is U, not '-'.

findings.name: Lure sensitivity predicts lower N-back accuracy across models (r = -.51 AR, -.32 TF)
Residual decodability and positional subspace overlap predict poorer recall; target readout alignment predicts recall
Projecting out letter-identity directions improves accuracy, mostly in weaker models (settings chosen and evaluated on the same 50 trials)
Load-dependent accuracy collapse persists under teacher forcing; target-selective heads spread attention to recent non-targets

xiong2026context.basis: The context is uncompressed with no budget, so Capacity does not arise; that follows by construction and is not a formal bound. The 2-layer solver bounds reader expressivity, not a store (Sec. 3 is right; Sec. 5's 'zero (B)' must go). Interference is I because the evidence is correlational and the projection was tuned and tested on the same 50 trials with no held-out set. Load and attention-spread effects confound Addressing and Interference.

findings.name: 4K+retrieval matches 16K long context; truncated 4K baselines are worst
Llama2-70B shows lost-in-the-middle; the long-context model uses top-5 retrieved context better
Adding retrieved chunks up to 20 does not help and sometimes hurts, even when they fit

xu2023retrieval.basis: This is an empirical comparison of several retrievers and context windows with no writer of its own, so query knowledge is '--'. It varies both tokens and k. Retrieval beating truncation at 4K is a policy comparison with no item-level evidence (rule 5: I). The more-chunks result confounds positional under-use with dilution, so it is Unassigned (Addressing, Interference). Revision: the study reports loss at a reduced budget against a larger one, which confounds Capacity, so Capacity is U, not '-'.

findings.name: At CR 0.9 JACAP beats CapKV (44.59 vs 39.53 on Qwen3-14B), with smaller leads on Qwen3-8B and Llama3.1-8B; CapKV wins at low compression
Heuristic eviction (KNorm, KeyDiff) collapses to about 20 versus a full-cache 47.48 at CR 0.9

yang2026jacap.basis: It scores tokens with the mean of past queries, which makes it proxy-query. Under rule 5 its same-budget wins lack item-level evidence and a count-matched control, so they are Addressing I with the confound that its diversity term may win by dropping redundant competitors. Comparisons with the full cache, and its 'information capacity' surrogate, do not bound the best store, so they are Unassigned (Capacity, Addressing).

findings.name: CapKV has the best LongBench average at every compression ratio on Qwen3-8B/14B (e.g. 39.53 vs SnapKV 37.13 at CR 0.9, Qwen3-14B)
Retained log-det capacity correlates with Qasper score (Spearman 0.75-0.86) across methods and ratios
Structure-only heuristics collapse at CR 0.9 (KeyDiff 20.95, Knorm 20.09 vs full 47.48)

yang2026rethinking.basis: The weights w_i use the mean of past queries, so CapKV is proxy-query. The draft cites it only to define query-agnostic, which is not a label for CapKV itself. Its policy wins are Addressing I under rule 5 (no item-level evidence; it may win by dropping redundant competitors). The capacity correlation mixes budgets and methods with a surrogate that does not bound the best store, so it is Unassigned (Capacity, Addressing).

findings.name: Merging evicted values into neighbours by attention-weighted convex combination alters retained values
Outperforms all baselines, especially at low budget ratios

yuan2025weightedkv.basis: Read only in abstract, so no cell can be above I. It scores tokens with averaged observed attention, which makes it proxy-query. Under rule 4, folded values leave the neighbouring entries present but altered, so this is Write distortion (I), not Interference as its placement in Sec. 5 implies. Its wins change both what is kept and what is written, so they are Unassigned (Addressing, Write distortion). Revision: the study reports loss at a reduced budget against a larger one, which confounds Capacity, so Capacity is U, not '-'.

findings.name: Neural LAM collapses at N=75 (1.3%) while KO stays at 100%
Higher semantic density rho moves collapse to smaller N
Multi-hop in neural memory: 100% isolated (N=6), 0% under load (N=106)
Neural updates fail (0% new value) and corrupt other facts (1.1% preserved)
Hopfield collapses with scale (0.5% at N=16,309) vs gradual KO decline
Structured facts beat raw text about 11x at Top-1
Dense scientific data: KO hash 100%, KO embedding 28%, neural 0.02%
Collapse extends to image embeddings (0.05% at N=2,000)
Schema drift in LLM extraction, even within one session
Corrections leave old and new values coexisting (version ambiguity)
In-context retrieval at N<=100 perfect, no positional bias

zahn2026attention.basis: The ledger puts extracted facts and triples under natural-language text however they are later retrieved, so the introduction's external-index placement is overridden. Interference is I because the density sweep does not hold the item and competitor count fixed. Write is M because Table 9 measures extraction drift directly. The KO-vs-neural and N-scaling contrasts confound Capacity, Interference and Write, so they are Unassigned. Stale versions that are retained and read go to Interference under rule 3. Revision: the study reports loss at a reduced budget against a larger one, which confounds Capacity, so Capacity is U, not '-'. Revision: hash lookup versus embedding search over the same facts at the same count re-keys every competitor, the Interference test of Section 2.2, so Interference is M; the density sweep alone would be I. Revision (2026-10-25, outside review): hashing also re-keys the target and replaces similarity search with exact lookup on a parsed subject and predicate, so the target is not held fixed and the hash-versus-embedding contrast changes Addressing with Interference (Unassigned); Interference stays I on the density sweep. Write distortion is I: schema drift is observed without an intervention or a measured loss.

findings.name: Mixed memory with iterative retrieval best on multi-hop QA
Full context beats all retrieval memories on QuALITY (81.5 vs 79.5)
Triples lose narrative context (QuALITY ~60 vs chunks ~77)
Summaries beat full content on NarrativeQA
No single structure best; mixed lowest on LoCoMo EM
Too many retrieved memories (K=200, R>50) lower scores
All structures degrade as noise documents are added
Memory-Doc helps broad-context tasks, not precision tasks

zeng2024structural.basis: The study is an analysis that evaluates several writers, so query knowledge is not applicable and there is no reuse flag. Raising K or adding noise documents raises access to the item and adds competitors at the same time, so those results are Unassigned (Addressing, Interference). Triple loss is graded I as write distortion, since format also changes the retrieval units. This follows the ledger's thin-evidence rule for text memory.

findings.name: 8-bit near lossless, 4-bit mild, 2-bit collapses at fixed tokens
At equal memory, cutting tokens hurts more than cutting precision
Quantized pruning gains on RULER at 1/16 budget (67.5 to 82.2)
Throughput-matched: 512 tokens at 4-bit beats 128 at 16-bit
Reasoning-heavy tasks gain less or prefer fewer, more precise tokens
8-bit/2x wins at high budget, 4-bit/4x at low budget
Smaller quantization groups lower loss
Per-channel KIVI beats token-wise FlexGen

zhang2025more.basis: The bit sweep at a fixed token count isolates write distortion (M). The token-for-precision gain is a same-budget policy comparison with no item-level evidence, so under rule 5 Addressing is I. The confound is that keeping more tokens also changes the competitor set. The pruners score tokens at prefill with the question in the prompt, so the writer is query-aware. Query knowledge is labelled by design: an observation-window scorer is proxy-query even when an evaluation puts the question inside the window. Revision: the study reports loss at a reduced budget against a larger one, which confounds Capacity, so Capacity is U, not '-'. Revision: the bit sweep at a fixed token count also lowers the bit budget, so Write distortion is U (Capacity, Write distortion), not M; the token-for-precision trade changes which tokens are kept and how precisely, so Addressing is U (Addressing, Write distortion). Query knowledge is labelled by design: the observation-window scorers are proxy-query.

findings.name: MixKVQ near BF16 on Qwen-32B reasoning; 2-bit KIVI drops
KVQuant collapses at 2-bit on reasoning (0 on AIME)
Key precision matters more than value precision (K4V2 6.81 vs K2V4 8.13)
Query magnitude weakly correlated with key scale (r=0.16)
Near-lossless LongBench at about 2.7 bits
Low-bit error accumulation flips long-CoT answers

zhang2026mixkvq.basis: The matched-bit key/value contrast isolates write distortion (M). The 2-bit reasoning collapse and error accumulation do not separate Capacity from Write distortion, so they are Unassigned, as in the draft table. Salience uses observed query-activation statistics as a stand-in for future reads, so despite the title the writer is proxy-query.

thiswork.operation: protect item; vary competitors; approximate index

findings.name: Query-aware eviction: keeping the answer-bearing item at the same budget repairs 99.8% (Task 1) and 63% (Task 2) of query-aware C-to-W rows; a count-matched sham repairs 2.0% and 6.5%
Protected query-aware stores within the budget bound the capacity floor: no loss against the full cache on Task 1; about zero on Task 2 at a 25% budget
Proxy-query and query-agnostic eviction: the same repair is Unassigned (Capacity, Addressing)
Full cache: near-duplicate keys lower accuracy from 98.3% to 81.1% as records grow from 200 to 1,400; 44 of 48 errors return another near-duplicate's value; same-category keys cause no errors
HotpotQA: question-similar distractors raise the odds of error with the item present, OR 1.44 (full cache) and 1.31 (compressed, item protected)
Token-retention thresholds do not mark readability: 31-43% of TOVA answers on Task 1 are correct below the half-the-tokens threshold (31-45% under stricter definitions)
HNSW search misses at the same k: restoring the lost gold paragraph repairs 73% of C->W rows vs 13% for a sham
48-byte codes at equal budget: gold recall 61% (sign bits), 68% (PQ), 71% (OPQ)

thiswork.basis: KV caches (Section 9): protection forces the answer-bearing item into the cache at the same budget and policy, and a count-matched sham that protects an equal-length non-answer span repairs almost nothing, so the repair comes from keeping the item. For query-aware runs the question determines the item, so the protected store is one the writer's class could build: the repair is a selection shortfall under rule 1 (Addressing M); the protected store's loss is an empirical upper bound on the capacity floor, which is not graded B, so Capacity stays U. For proxy-query and query-agnostic runs the repair is Unassigned (Capacity, Addressing). Competitor similarity is varied at a fixed count with the item present (Interference M), for two readers on Task 1. External index (Section 7): HNSW changes only the search at the same k, and restoring the lost gold paragraph repairs C->W rows beyond a count-matched sham (Addressing M); codes of equal size compared under exact search change only how keys are written (Write distortion M); quantized versus float vectors also change the budget (Unassigned).
